The trapThe project team is all people allocating time to it; the management team is board, manager, assurance, support.

Promappsoftware

A tool specifically for storing and maintaining an organisation's , so they stay findable and up to date rather than dying in someone's folder.

In the proper languageNintex Promapp. process management platform providing a central process repository with ownership, versioning and review cycles.

Prototypestechnique

Showing someone a rough version of the thing. People who cannot describe what they want will immediately tell you what is wrong with something in front of them.

In the proper language and technique using low- or high-fidelity mock-ups to make abstract tangible and surface unstated expectations.

Proximityconcept

What is near feels more dangerous than what is far off.

In the proper language“A mindset where situations that are closer in time are seen as riskier and more important than those in the future.”

Purpose, objectives and contextconcept

Three different questions: why it exists, what it achieves, when it runs.

In the proper language

Purpose
Why the process exists, in one sentence.
Objectives
The specific things it must achieve — usually a list beginning “to ensure that…”.
Context
When it runs, what triggers it, who leads it, and how it relates to the others.

The trapPurpose is why it exists; an objective is a thing it must achieve.

Qualityaspect

How good the thing has to be, decided and written down before it gets built rather than argued about afterwards.

In the proper languageAn aspect of project performance. The quality practice exists “to document the user’s requirements of the project products and to establish the means by which they will be met”. A quality tolerance is “the permissible deviation in a product’s quality before escalation is needed”.

Quality (the practice)practice

The part of the work that settles what would count as done properly, and how that gets checked.

In the proper language

“To document the user’s requirements of the project products and to establish the means by which they will be met.”

It “addresses the quality concepts, guidance, techniques, management products, and responsibilities for the project products”, and “quality is concerned with ensuring that the project products meet the user’s requirements and expectations and enable the desired to be realized”.

DangerA great deal of the material in circulation gives the purpose as “to ensure products are fit for purpose”. True in spirit, and not the wording. The purpose is to document the user’s requirements of the project products and to establish the means by which they will be met.

Quality assuranceconcept

An outside check on how the job is run — the way of working, not the things made.

In the proper language

An independent check that the project is being run properly — a check on the process, usually performed from outside the project team, for example by a corporate or programme function.

Distinguish it from : “project board members are accountable for the assurance of their respective areas of concern (business assurance, user assurance, supplier assurance)”.

The trapQuality assurance checks the process, from outside; project assurance is the project board’s own.

Quality controlconcept

Checking the things that were built, against the standard set for them.

In the proper language“The procedures to monitor the specific products of a project and their development or delivery activities to determine whether they comply with relevant standards and of identifying ways to minimize causes of unsatisfactory performance.” Activities are recorded in the , “starting with the approval of each product description”.

Quality management approachapproach

How quality will be handled across the job — the methods, the standards, and who does what.

In the proper language

“To describe the quality techniques and standards to be applied and the roles and responsibilities for achieving the required quality specifications and acceptance criteria during a project.” Held in the .

“The quality management approach should focus on how quality control will be organized, performed, monitored, and reported while providing a concise explanation of how quality planning has occurred.”

Quality planningconcept

Setting the standard before anything is built.

In the proper languageQuality planning sets the criteria. Its primary input is the , which “should identify all the major products to be delivered”.

Quality registerdocument

The record of every check planned or done, and how each one turned out.

In the proper language“To summarize all quality management activities that are planned or have occurred.” Used by the and as part of reviewing progress.

Quality specificationsdefinition

How good one particular thing has to be, and how that is measured.

In the proper language“A description of the quality measures that will be applied by those performing and the levels that a finished product must meet.” They are stated in .

The trapExpectations and acceptance criteria are the whole project; specifications are one product.

Quality tolerancedefinition

How far off the standard a thing may be before someone above has to be told.

In the proper language“The permissible deviation in a product’s quality that is allowed before the deviation needs to be escalated to the next level of management.” Stated in the .

Quality: planning against control against assuranceconcept

The standard, the things, the way of working.

In the proper language

Sets the criteria.
Checks the products.
Checks the process, independently.

RACInot in your notestechnique

A grid saying, for each task, who does it, who signs it off, who gets consulted and who just needs telling. Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed.

In the proper languageResponsibility assignment matrix distinguishing Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed parties per activity or deliverable.

RAID logdocument

A single list tracking four kinds of thing that could derail a project: Risks, Assumptions, Issues and Dependencies.

In the proper languageA working convention rather than a defined in any method — PRINCE2 has no RAID log, splitting the same ground across separate registers inside the .

Raising the exception report (exception step 2)technique

Warn them, and say what could be done.

In the proper languageIf a stage tolerance is forecast to be breached, the project manager raises an to the , setting out the cause, the options and a recommendation.

Recommending (issue step 3)technique

Set out the options and say which one.

In the proper languageOptions are identified and a recommendation made to whoever holds the authority to decide.

Reduce (threat response)concept

Make it less likely, or less bad, or both.

In the proper languageAlso called mitigate. Lower the , the , or both.

Regression testingtechnique

Re-checking things that already worked, to make sure the new change hasn't broken them. Dull, and the thing that saves you most often.

In the proper languageRe-execution of existing against unchanged functionality following a change, to detect unintended side effects. Commonly automated given repetition.

Regulatory and compliance awarenessnot in your notesprocess

Knowing which laws and industry rules constrain what you're allowed to build. In financial services, healthcare or government this shapes before anyone starts designing.

In the proper languageAwareness of statutory and sector-specific obligations — data protection, financial conduct, accessibility, records retention — that constrain design and generate mandatory non-functional requirements.

Reject (opportunity response)concept

Let the chance go by without doing anything about it.

In the proper languageTake no action to capture it. Mirrors .

Release managementrole

The team that controls what actually goes live, when, and what happens if it goes wrong. Even finished work waits for them.

In the proper languageThe practice of planning, scheduling and controlling the movement of releases into test and live environments, including rollback planning and .

Reports and standalone productsdocument

Everything that travels, rather than sits in a folder.

In the proper language

  • — project, stage, team or exception

Request for changedefinition

Somebody asking for something agreed to be altered.

In the proper language“A proposal for a change to a baseline.”

Requirementdefinition

Something wanted, written down and agreed.

In the proper language“A need or expectation that is documented in an approved management product.”

Requirements decompositionnot in your notestechnique

The actual craft of turning a broad business need into buildable pieces. “Customers should feel informed” becomes a , then several , then a set of technical . Each level gets more precise and each traces back to the one above.

In the proper languageProgressive elaboration of high-level business needs into functional and technical , maintaining bidirectional at each level of decomposition.

This is the process behind Daniel’s margin note — “turning into bus / tech req spec”.

Requirements engineeringprocess

The whole business of working out what needs building — finding it out, writing it down, checking it, and keeping control of it as things change. It's called engineering because you construct requirements out of vague and contradictory statements; they don't exist ready-made.

In the proper languageThe systematic discipline covering , , , and management of across a lifecycle, including and .

Requirements gatheringprocess

A very common phrase for the same activity. Slightly misleading, because gathering suggests the answers are lying about waiting to be picked up. They usually have to be worked out.

In the proper languageColloquial term for . Often deprecated in favour of “”, which better reflects that are constructed rather than collected.

Requirements traceability matrixdocument

A table linking every forward through the whole chain — from the business need that prompted it, to the that describes it, to the test that proves it, to the that accepts it. It exists to prove nothing quietly went missing.

In the proper languageMatrix mapping each requirement bidirectionally to its source business need and to downstream design, build and test , enabling coverage and impact assessment.

Reviewerrole

Whoever decides whether it passed.

In the proper language“The person or group responsible for assessing if a product meets its quality or acceptance criteria.” Within controlling quality, the reviewer is the person doing the checking.

Reviewing and reporting progress and lessonsconcept

Check in regularly, and write down what you learn.

In the proper language

“As part of the ‘’ process, the project manager will regularly review progress through checkpoint reports and will maintain the .”

A is “information to facilitate the future of the project or other projects and actively promote learning from experience”.

Riskdefinition

Something that might happen and would matter if it did.

In the proper language“An uncertain event or set of events that, should they occur, will affect the achievement of objectives.” Measured by “a combination of the probability of a perceived threat or opportunity occurring and the magnitude of its impact on objectives”.

Risk (the practice)practice

The part of the work that deals with what might happen, good or bad.

In the proper language

“To identify, assess, and control uncertainties that would affect the project’s objectives, and, as a result, improve the ability of the project to succeed.”

Improve the ability to succeed. “There is no guarantee that the agreed objectives would be met.”

The trapNot only about avoiding bad things — risk covers threats and opportunities.

Risk action ownerrole

Whoever carries out one agreed response. It need not be the same person.

In the proper language“The nominated owner of agreed actions to respond to a risk. This role is also known as the risk actionee.” May be the same person as the , or not.

The trapThe owner manages the whole risk; the action owner owns one agreed action.

Risk appetitedefinition

How much risk the organisation will run to get what it wants.

In the proper languageThe organization’s attitude towards risk-taking — how much risk it is willing to accept in pursuit of its objectives.

The trapAppetite is an attitude, organization-wide; tolerance is a measurable threshold.

Risk budgetdefinition

Money set aside for dealing with risks when they turn up.

In the proper language“A sum of money to fund specific management responses to the project’s threats and opportunities (for example, to cover the costs of any contingent plans should a risk materialize).”

Risk categories and PESTLEtechnique

Sorting risks into kinds stops whole types being missed.

In the proper language“The use of risk categories helps projects to identify and prioritize risks. Techniques such as (Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, and Environmental) can be used to analyse the internal and external context for risks and help to identify different types of risk that may affect the project.”

Risk cause, event and effectconcept

Where it comes from, what might happen, and what it would do.

In the proper language

Cause
The existing situation that gives rise to it.
Event
The uncertain thing that may happen.
Effect
The impact on objectives if it does.

Risk exposuredefinition

How much of what you want is at stake right now.

In the proper language“The degree to which a particular objective is at risk.”

Risk impactdefinition

How much damage or good it would do if it happened.

In the proper language“The estimated effect on objectives should a risk occur.”

Risk management approachapproach

How risk will be handled on this job — written down before any risk is found.

In the proper language“To describe how risk will be managed on the project. This includes the specific procedures, techniques, standards, and responsibilities to be applied.” Held in the .

Risk or issue?concept

Has it happened yet? That is the whole test.

In the proper language

Uncertain, not yet happened
Unplanned, has happened

The trapUncertain and not yet happened is a risk; unplanned and already happened is an issue.

Risk ownerrole

The person answerable for one whole risk.

In the proper language“The person who is responsible for the management, monitoring, and control of all aspects of a particular risk assigned to them, including the implementation of the selected responses to address the threats or to maximize the opportunities.”

Risk probabilitydefinition

How likely it is to happen at all.

In the proper language“The probability that the risk will occur (often estimated by considering its likelihood or frequency).”

Risk registerdocument

The list of what might happen, good or bad, and what is being done about each one.

In the proper language“A record of identified risks related to the project, including their status and history. It is used to capture and maintain information on all the identified threats and opportunities relating to the project.”

Risk tolerancedefinition

The agreed range a risk may move within before somebody senior has to be told.

In the proper language“A measurable threshold to represent the tolerable range of outcomes for each objective ‘at risk’, using the same units as for measuring performance for that objective.”

Role descriptionsdocument

What each named job answers for, written down.

In the proper languageDescribe “the roles of those in the project management team and their specific responsibilities”. These “should include specific accountability for targets”. Held in the .

Role-baseddefinition

Responsibility attaches to named jobs rather than to whoever happens to be free, so it is always clear who answers for what.

In the proper languageOne of the four structural features of PRINCE2, following from the define roles, responsibilities and relationships principle: the project has defined and agreed roles within a structure engaging the business, user and supplier interests.

Roles personalized, not standardizedrole

A job is shaped around the person holding it, and reshaped when the people around them change.

In the proper language

“Roles and responsibilities should reflect the capability, authority, and availability of the individual undertaking the work and should be considered through the lens of their key relationships. They should be reviewed in the event of any shifts in these key relationships and updated accordingly.”

The consequence: generic, standard are unlikely to be effective.

Root cause analysisnot in your notestechnique

Digging past the obvious symptom to find what actually caused a problem, so you fix the cause rather than the same symptom over and over.

In the proper languageStructured investigation identifying the underlying origin of a fault or failure rather than its presenting symptoms, using techniques such as , fishbone or fault tree analysis.

SAFenot in your notesprocess

A framework for running across many teams at once in a big organisation. Scaled Agile Framework. Turns up constantly on job adverts for large employers.

In the proper languageScaled Framework. Prescriptive model for coordinating multiple agile teams via Agile Release Trains, Program Increment planning and defined portfolio-level roles.

Same capability, different performanceconcept

Two people trained the same will not do the job the same way, and the same person varies with who they work with.

In the proper language“Even when people technically have the same capabilities and competencies, they are likely to perform the same role differently. Sometimes, the same person may perform differently depending on who they are working with.”

SAPsoftware

A very large German software company whose runs the back office of a lot of big organisations. Notoriously complex.

In the proper languageEnterprise software vendor. SAP and S/4HANA are widely deployed in large-enterprise finance, supply chain and manufacturing.

Scheduleconcept

What happens in what order, and for how long.

In the proper language“The sequencing, interrelationships, and duration of and their associated tasks are captured in a schedule. All work packages for a stage must be included in the schedule for the stage.”

Scopeconcept

Everything the plan says will be done — including the managing of it, not just the making.

In the proper language“The sum of product, delivery, and management activities represented by an approved plan and its and .”

The trapBroader than products plus the work — management activities are inside it.

Scope creepdefinition

Extra work quietly getting added without anyone formally agreeing to it. Not usually anyone being difficult — just lots of small “can it also just…” requests that never got written down.

In the proper languageUncontrolled expansion of scope through unmanaged additions; PRINCE2 calls this uncontrolled change and prevents it by updating a plan only once a change has been approved.

Scrumprocess

The most common specific way of doing . Work happens in fixed short blocks with a defined set of meetings and three defined roles.

In the proper language framework structuring delivery into fixed-length with prescribed roles (, , Developers), events and .

Scrum Masterrole

The person responsible for the process running properly and for clearing obstacles out of the team's way. Not a manager of people.

In the proper language role accountable for the framework being understood and enacted, facilitating events, coaching the team and removing impediments.

SDLCprocess

The whole journey a piece of software goes through, from someone first having the idea to the day it gets switched off. Software Development Life Cycle. It's the container; and are two different ways of moving through it.

In the proper languageSoftware Development Life Cycle. The sequence of phases — typically initiation, , design, build, test, deploy, operate, retire — within which a delivery methodology operates.

Senior supplierrole

The person answerable for the thing being sound, and for the people building it.

In the proper language“Accountable for the quality of the products delivered by the suppliers and for the technical integrity of the project.”

Senior userrole

The person answerable for it being what was needed, and for it being taken up afterwards.

In the proper language“Accountable for ensuring that user needs are specified correctly and that the solution meets those needs.” Also responsible for “the successful handover and adoption of products into the business and continued realization of benefits after the project has closed”, and for securing ongoing commitment from the user community.

Seniority across the structureconcept

Someone on the team may outrank the person running the work, which is normal and makes for friction.

In the proper language

“It is not unusual for members of the project team to be more senior than the , potentially causing hierarchical tension.”

And: “some motivational factors may be outside of a project manager’s remit — for example, remuneration and career progression of project team members.”

Service-level agreementdocument

A written promise about how quickly problems will be responded to and fixed once the thing is live, usually with penalties attached if it's missed.

In the proper languageFormal agreement defining measurable service targets — availability, response and resolution times by — together with reporting and remedies for breach.

ServiceNownot in your notessoftware

A large platform for running IT service desks and workflows — where , requests and changes get logged and tracked. The system that practices usually run inside.

In the proper languageEnterprise service management platform providing ITSM workflows for incident, problem, change and request management, plus workflow automation across other functions.

Setting and verifying baselinesconcept

Decide how finely to pin things down, then check now and then that they still match.

In the proper language

“Regardless of size, scale, and complexity, the project management team needs to determine: the appropriate level at which the products need to be baselined.”

“It is good practice to periodically verify that the actual status of the products reflects the authorized state of products and look for any discrepancies.”

Severitydefinition

How badly the thing is broken. A technical judgement about the damage.

In the proper languageClassification of the technical impact of a on system function, independent of business urgency.

Share (threat and opportunity response)concept

Both sides take the gain and the pain.

In the proper languageBoth parties share gain and pain. The only response that appears in both columns.

SharePointsoftware

Microsoft's system for storing and sharing documents inside a company. Where the end up.

In the proper languageMicrosoft platform for document management, collaboration and intranet sites, with versioning and permission control.

Should have

Painful to go without, but you would still ship.

In the proper languageImportant but not vital ; omission causes significant inconvenience for which a workaround exists.

Sign-offprocess

The formal moment someone with authority accepts the work. It matters because it is the point where responsibility transfers.

In the proper languageDocumented acceptance that a meets its criteria; in acceptance typically transfers ownership or responsibility from the project or supplier to the , on behalf of the user.

Solid Edge CADsoftware

Siemens engineering design software, used for drawing physical in 3D. Nothing to do with — it tells you which industry that person worked in.

In the proper languageSiemens application for mechanical design. Sector-specific rather than a competency.

Solutiondefinition

Whatever gets built or changed to fix the problem. It does not have to be software — a solution might be a new process, some training, or scrapping a step entirely. Analysts say “solution” rather than “system” deliberately, because assuming the answer is software is the most common early mistake in the job.

In the proper languageThe set of changes to process, people, technology or policy that satisfies a defined business need. Deliberately technology-agnostic terminology, reflecting that should precede solution selection.

Solution architectrole

The person who decides how something will be built technically — which systems, which approach, how the pieces connect. You decide what it must do; they decide how.

In the proper languageRole responsible for the technical design of a within a specific initiative, translating into a technical approach consistent with .

Specialist productdocument

The thing the work actually exists to produce, as opposed to the paperwork that keeps it under control.

In the proper languageA product the project exists to deliver, as distinct from a . Both kinds sit in the once approved.

Specificationdocument

A written description precise enough to build from. The test is simple: could two people read it separately and produce the same thing? If not, it is not a specification yet — it is a wish.

In the proper languageA document defining the required characteristics of a deliverable in unambiguous, verifiable terms. Forms the basis for build and the reference against which acceptance is judged.

Sprintprocess

A fixed block of time, usually two weeks, in which a team commits to finishing an agreed amount of work. Once it starts, nothing new gets added.

In the proper languageTime-boxed iteration of fixed duration producing a potentially releasable increment. Sprint is protected from change once committed.

SQLdefinition

The language used to ask questions of a database. Structured Query Language. A doesn't usually need to write much, but being able to check a number yourself rather than waiting three days for someone else to check it is a genuine advantage.

In the proper languageStructured Query Language. Declarative language for querying and manipulating relational . For analysts, principally used for data profiling, and reconciliation.

Stagedefinition

A chunk of work somebody senior has approved you to get on with. At the end of each one you go back for permission to start the next, which is also the moment the whole thing can be stopped.

In the proper languageThe section of a project the is managing on behalf of the at any one time; there are always at least two.

Stage plandocument

The next chunk of work in detail, close enough to see clearly.

In the proper language

“A detailed plan used as the basis for project management control throughout a stage”, “based on more precise estimates that are achievable within the ”.

Prepared near the end of the previous stage, by the .

Stageddefinition

The work is broken into chunks, and permission to start the next one is given only at the end of the last.

In the proper languageOne of the four structural features of PRINCE2, following from the manage by stages principle: the project is planned, monitored and controlled on a stage-by-stage basis.

Stages on an iterative-incremental projectconcept

When the work is done in rounds, there are more delivery stages and the standard firms up as you go.

In the proper language“For an project, the may provide multiple delivery stages in which the quality and acceptance criteria are refined in parallel with development of the required products through the use of a product backlog.”

Stakeholderconcept

Anyone the work touches, anyone who can touch the work, and anyone who merely believes they are affected.

In the proper language

A stakeholder is “any individual, group, or organization that can affect or be affected by (or perceives itself to be affected by) the project”.

They sit inside or outside the business — “trade unions, customers, suppliers, communities, interest groups, banks, or the media”.

The trapNotes routinely drop “or perceives itself to be affected by”. Without that clause the definition is wrong.

Stakeholder engagementtechnique

Work out who cares, how much they count, what to tell them, tell them — then check whether any of it landed.

In the proper language

  • Identifying stakeholders
  • Analysing their interests and influence
  • Planning how to communicate with them
  • Engaging
  • Measuring whether the engagement is working

STARtechnique

Situation, Task, Action, Result. A structure for answering interview questions about your experience. It is not a technique, despite appearing on a CV as though it were.

In the proper languageBehavioural response framework. Not an method; its appearance as an “analysis framework” is a misattribution.

From Gabrielle's CV. Listed there as an analysis framework, which it isn't.

Starting up a project (SU)process

Is this worth bothering with at all? — asked before anyone has permission to start.

In the proper language

“To ensure that the prerequisites for ‘initiating a project’ are established by answering the question, ‘Do we have a viable and worthwhile project?’ The decision to start the project must be explicit, as the activities within the process of starting up a project happen before this decision.”

“The purpose of the process of starting up a project is as much about preventing poorly conceived ideas from ever being initiated as it is about progressing viable projects for approval… The aim is to do the minimum necessary to decide whether it is worthwhile to even initiate the project.”

Pre-project, led by the or . Triggered by the . Ends with a request to the to initiate the project.

The trapIt happens before there is authority to proceed.

Supplier interestconcept

The side doing the building, whether they are in-house or hired in.

In the proper languageThose providing the skills and resources to build the products. They “may come from within the organization, or external suppliers may be used for their skills and knowledge”. Represented by the .

Surveystechnique

Sending questions out to a lot of people at once. Wide but shallow: good for counting how common something is, bad for understanding why.

In the proper languageQuantitative technique offering broad coverage at low depth. Useful for hypotheses across a large population rather than generating them.

Sustainabilityaspect

Whether what you build stands up environmentally and socially. Judged and limited exactly like cost or time.

In the proper languageThe seventh aspect of project performance and a full area, documented in the , referencing the organization’s environmental, social and governance () goals.

Sustainability management approachapproach

How the work will keep track of its effect on the planet and on people, and report on it.

In the proper languageHow the project’s environmental, social and economic objectives will be managed, measured and reported. Held in the .

Swimlanesnot in your notesdefinition

Horizontal bands across a process diagram, one per person or team. They show who does what — and every point where work crosses from one band to another is a handover, which is where things usually go wrong.

In the proper language construct partitioning a process by participant or role. Cross-lane transitions represent handoffs and are common sites of delay and error.

Tableausoftware

A rival to doing much the same job — turning data into charts and dashboards.

In the proper languageData visualisation and business intelligence platform, strong on exploratory visual of large datasets.

Tailor to suit the projectprinciple

The method gets sized to the job in hand, so a small job gets a lighter version of it.

In the proper language

“PRINCE2 Project Management is applied and tailored to suit the project environment, size, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and level of risk.”

The purpose of doing so: “to ensure that project controls are appropriate to the project’s scale, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and risk”.

The trapManage by exception sets tolerances and limits of authority; tailor makes the method itself proportionate. If the sentence mentions a threshold, a limit or escalation, it is manage by exception.

Tailoringconcept

Fitting the method to the job instead of bending the job to fit the method.

In the proper language

“To enable PRINCE2 Project Management to be used for such a wide range of projects, the method is flexible in how it can be used for any given project. Rather than prescribing what to do to align the method to the specific project, PRINCE2 Project Management offers guidance through principles.”

Tailoring “supports the ability to adapt the PRINCE2 Project Management method to the people and organizations involved, rather than attempting to adapt them to the method”. The principles themselves are “likely to be applied in different ways across projects within an organization”.

Tailoring the management productsdocument

The paperwork can be merged together, or written in a different shape.

In the proper language can be combined with one another, and their format changed.

Tailoring the processesconcept

The steps can be made shorter, or fuller.

In the proper languageProcesses can be tailored by simplifying them or by elaborating them.

Tailoring the project controlsconcept

How closely the work is watched, and how often it has to report back.

In the proper languageThe project controls themselves can be tailored, “to ensure that project controls are appropriate to the project’s scale, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and risk”.

Tailoring the rolesrole

One person can hold more than one job, up to a point.

In the proper languageRoles can be combined, within limits — creating “a project management team that is appropriate to the needs of the project and the capability of the organizations and people involved”.

Tailoring the terminologyconcept

The words can be swapped for the ones people here already use.

In the proper languageTerminology can be tailored — the method’s words replaced by “what is common in the company or in the industry in which the project is taking place”.

Tasks

The boxes on the diagram. One thing that someone does.

In the proper languageAtomic activity within a representing work performed by a participant.

Team managerrole

Whoever runs one patch of the building work. The job can be left unfilled.

In the proper languageDelivers “the products to the agreed specifications”. “Coordinates an area of work that will deliver one or more of the that form the .” May be internal or external.

The trapOptional — the project manager can do it.

Team plandocument

One team’s plan for one parcel of work. It can be skipped.

In the proper language

“A plan used as the basis for organizing and controlling the work of a team when executing a .”

Produced by the .

The trapOptional — the only level that is.

Temporarycharacteristic

It has a start and a finish, and then it stops existing.

In the proper language“Projects are temporary in nature. When the desired change has been implemented, resumes (in its new form), and the need for the project is removed.” Because they are temporary “they should therefore have a defined start and a defined end”.

Temporary organizationconcept

A group of people brought together to get one thing done, and taken apart again once it is. Not a department and not a permanent team.

In the proper languageThe phrase the definition of a project turns on. A project is a temporary organization created to deliver one or more business products according to an agreed business case — a structure of people, not merely a piece of work.

Test casedocument

One specific thing to try, with what you expect to happen written down beforehand.

In the proper languageA defined set of preconditions, inputs, execution steps and expected results used to verify a specific or behaviour.

The board’s options (exception step 3)technique

Accept, reject, move the limits, or go higher.

In the proper language

“The project board or have several options that they could take.”

  • Accept or reject the recommendation
  • They “may reallocate the overall project tolerances to resolve the breach of the stage tolerance”
  • Request an
  • Escalate “to the for advice and direction, if the exception will take the project outside one or more of its project level tolerances”

The trapNever the project manager’s options.

The business case lifecycleconcept

Written before the work, checked all the way through, and looked at again once it is over.

In the proper language

The is used to develop the outline business case, which sits inside the .
The outline is developed into the full business case and baselined as part of the .
During each stage
The keeps it under review — “the business case is kept under review” is an explicit objective of — and checks it when assessing progress, risks and issues.
At each
Updated with actual costs, products delivered, benefits realized and the latest forecasts, so the can confirm continued justification before approving the next stage.
Checked to “assess the project’s performance against requirements and the probability that the outcomes will provide the expected benefits”. Any remaining benefit reviews are handed to the business in the .
After closure
Reviewed by the business in a post-project , to confirm whether the intended benefits were realized in practice.

The business case practice and the principlespractice

The seven practice purposes, side by sidepractice

Seven sentences, and every wrong answer is one of the other six.

In the proper language

To establish mechanisms to judge whether the project is (and remains) desirable, viable, and achievable as a means to support decision-making in its continued investment.
To define and establish the project’s structure of accountability and responsibilities (the “who”).
To facilitate communication and control by defining the products to be delivered and the means to deliver them, to satisfy the project business case.
To document the user’s requirements of the project products and to establish the means by which they will be met.
To identify, assess, and control uncertainties that would affect the project’s objectives and, as a result, improve the ability of the project to succeed.
To collect and assess issues and control changes to the project’s baseline.
To establish mechanisms to monitor and compare actual achievements against those planned; provide a forecast for the project’s objectives and continued viability; and control any deviations causing an exception.

Output → change → capability → outcome → benefit → business objective. A negative outcome gives a dis-benefit.

A different diagram language, for describing software rather than business processes. Unified Modeling Language. Where asks who does what, UML asks how the system is put together.

In the proper languageOMG standard notation for modelling software systems, comprising structural diagrams (class, component) and behavioural diagrams (sequence, state, activity).

Doing the strictly one after another: work everything out, write it all down, build it all, test it all, release it. Changing your mind late is expensive, because everything downstream was built on the earlier decisions.

Product status

Where tailoring decisions are documenteddocument

In the folder agreed before the real money is spent — the .

In the proper language

“How PRINCE2 Project Management will be applied and tailored for the particular project is captured in the .”

The trapThe , the and the are all three offered as wrong answers.

Who is responsible for tailoringrole

The person running the work proposes it; the people who authorise the work agree it.

In the proper language

“The is responsible for tailoring and will make recommendations having consulted relevant lessons and standards.”

The project manager proposes; the , as the body accountable for the project, agrees the approach as part of approving the .

Who reports what to whomdocument

Every report goes one step up the chain, and is either on a clock or on an event.

In the proper language

→ . Time-driven — frequency set in the .
→ . Time-driven — frequency set by the board.
→ . Event-driven — end of each stage.
→ . Event-driven — forecast tolerance breach.
→ . Event-driven — closure.
Escalation beyond project tolerance
→ . Event-driven — project tolerance forecast to be exceeded.

The trapCheckpoint and highlight are time-driven; end stage, exception and end project are event-driven.

Why project management is usedconcept

Change pushed through the normal chain of command fails in the same handful of ways every time.

In the proper language

Change delivered through normal line management tends to fail in predictable ways: unclear objectives and scope, no agreed justification, poor estimation, undefined roles, uncontrolled change, unmanaged risk, and stakeholders who were never engaged.

PRINCE2 addresses exactly those failure modes: a documented justification, defined roles across business, user and supplier, product definitions agreed before work starts, controlled with , and an explicit route for escalating problems.

WIP limitnot in your notesdefinition

A cap on how many jobs can be underway at the same time. Counter-intuitive but it makes things finish faster, because starting a fifth job doesn't make the first four go quicker.

In the proper languageWork-in-progress constraint applied per board column, used to expose bottlenecks and reduce cycle time by limiting concurrent work.

Wireframenot in your notesdocument

A deliberately rough sketch of a screen layout, showing where things go without any styling. Rough on purpose, so people comment on the structure rather than the colours.

In the proper languageLow-fidelity representation of interface layout and content hierarchy, excluding visual design to focus feedback on structure and flow.

Won't have

Agreed to be out of this time round. It does not mean never — and writing it down explicitly is what stops it quietly reappearing in three weeks.

In the proper language formally excluded from the current delivery but retained on record for potential future consideration.

Work breakdown structuretechnique

A map of the work, hanging off the products.

In the proper language“A hierarchy of all work to be done during a project that forms a link between the and the … supporting the project manager in determining how to structure project teams and the boundaries between them.”

The trapAn organizing concept, not a plans one, and its purpose is about structuring teams.

Work packagedocument

The parcel of work handed to a team, saying what to produce, to what standard, by when, and what to report back. It is the boundary between the person planning and the people building.

In the proper languageA description of the work handed to a team manager, defining the required, their , constraints, reporting arrangements and .

Work package descriptiondocument

One parcel of work, written down, and handed over formally.

In the proper language“To describe how one or more products will be produced and delivered. It is used to pass responsibility for work formally to a or team member.”

Workshop facilitationnot in your notestechnique

Running a meeting so it actually produces something. A named skill in its own right — keeping the loudest person from dominating, making sure the quiet expert gets heard, and ending with decisions rather than a nice chat.

In the proper languageThe practice of designing and running structured group sessions to reach defined , managing participation, conflict and decision-making without contributing content oneself.

Workshopstechnique

Getting a group in a room together. The real value is that disagreements surface early, while they are still cheap to resolve.

In the proper languageFacilitated group session. Efficient for reaching consensus and exposing conflicting , but requires active facilitation to avoid dominance by senior voices.

Sheet 20 · 160 cards

Premade cue cards

Key concepts 12

Name the five integrated elements of PRINCE2.

Principles, people, practices, processes, and the project context.

What is the PRINCE2 definition of a project?

A temporary organization created to deliver one or more business products according to an agreed business case.

Name the five characteristics of a project.

Change, temporary, cross-functional, unique, uncertainty (riskier than business as usual).

Name the seven aspects of project performance.

Benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability, risk.

Which aspect of performance did PRINCE2 7 add?

Sustainability.

Is “people” an aspect of project performance?

No — it is an integrated element. This is a deliberate exam distractor.

Name the three delivery approaches.

Linear-sequential, iterative-incremental, hybrid.

Is “event-driven” a delivery approach?

No. It is a type of control, from the progress practice.

Define project management.

Planning, delegating, monitoring and controlling all aspects of a project, and motivating those involved, to achieve the objectives within the expected performance targets.

Which element covers “those working on the project and those affected by the project”?

People.

Give two features or benefits of PRINCE2.

It is generic and not specific to any industry or delivery method; it provides a common vocabulary enabling reuse of assets and staff mobility; it separates management from specialist work; it is product-focused with controlled stages, defined roles and management by exception.

Can PRINCE2 terminology be tailored?

Yes — it may be adjusted to match terms used in the company, the industry, or the organizations involved.

Principles 16

How many principles are there, and must all be applied?

Seven, and unless all seven are applied it is not a PRINCE2 project.

List the seven principles.

Ensure continued business justification; learn from experience; define roles, responsibilities and relationships; manage by stages; manage by exception; focus on products; tailor to suit the project.

What does “ensure continued business justification” require?

Justification sufficient to warrant investment to initiate and to continue through to completion — revalidated throughout. If it does not exist, the project should be stopped.

What three time horizons does “learn from experience” cover?

Lessons from prior projects, lessons throughout this project, and lessons applied to future projects and shared with others.

What does the “define roles, responsibilities and relationships” principle require?

Defined and agreed roles and responsibilities within an organization structure that engages the business, user and supplier stakeholder interests.

Why does a project need its own structure rather than using line management?

“The day-to-day line management structures of the business may not be designed for, or suited to, project work.”

What does “manage by stages” require?

The project is planned, monitored and controlled on a stage-by-stage basis — minimum two stages.

Define a management stage.

The section of a project that the project manager is managing on behalf of the project board at any one time.

Explain “manage by exception”.

Establish limits of delegated authority by defining tolerances for performance against plans; escalate only when a tolerance is forecast to be breached.

What benefit does managing by exception give senior managers?

Efficient use of their time — it reduces their time burden without removing their control, so decisions are made at the right level.

What does “focus on products” mean?

The project focuses on the definition and delivery of products, in particular their user's quality expectations and requirements.

Name four factors that influence tailoring.

Any of: project environment, size, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability, level of risk (plus internal and external business factors).

Who is responsible for tailoring?

The project manager, who makes recommendations having consulted relevant lessons and standards.

Where are tailoring decisions documented?

In the PID — not the project plan, stage plan or business case.

Can practices be excluded if they are not relevant?

No. Practices must be applied consistently and throughout the lifecycle; what you adjust is how each one is treated, not whether it applies. An answer offering to drop a practice that is not relevant is wrong.

What is the direction of tailoring?

Adapt the method to the people and organizations involved, rather than attempting to adapt them to the method.

People 22

Distinguish the organizational ecosystem from the project ecosystem.

The organizational ecosystem is the wider organization(s) the project sits within; the project ecosystem is the project's own community of people, which develops as a distinct entity from it.

What is the business layer?

The layer of governance outside the project team that sets the overall objectives and tolerance levels for the project and holds the project board accountable.

How do people “within” the project differ from people “affected by” it?

Within = the project management team and those delivering the work. Affected by = people in the business affected by the project who do not work within the defined project team; they typically contribute by integrating new products into their area.

Is the senior user inside or outside the project team?

Inside. They represent the user community; they are not part of the “affected by” group.

What is change management in the people sense?

Establishing the target organizational state and the means by which the business shifts from the current state through any interim states.

How does change management differ from change control?

Change management moves the organization from current to target state so benefits are realized; change control governs modifications to baselined products (issues practice).

Define a stakeholder.

Any individual, group or organization that can affect or be affected by — or perceives itself to be affected by — the project.

Who are key influencers?

The people the project management team needs to work closest with to ensure the success of the project.

Do stakeholders stay the same throughout a project?

No — stakeholders at the interface with the project may change over time as the project evolves and relationships develop.

Define culture.

The set of shared attitudes, values and goals of a group.

Define collaboration.

People from across the project ecosystem working together to achieve the project's objectives.

Define co-creation.

A specific form of collaboration involving users and key influencers in the design of products and agreed ways of working, to ensure adoption by the project and organizational ecosystems.

Define leadership.

Motivating people to achieve a project's objectives — through collaboration, persuading, influencing and co-creating, managing key relationships and seeking regular feedback.

Define management.

Instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working.

On what are effective teams built?

A diverse set of capabilities, competencies and perspectives that match the requirements of the project.

Do identical capabilities produce identical performance?

No — people with the same capabilities and competencies are likely to perform the same role differently, and may perform differently depending on who they work with.

How should capability gaps be handled?

Identify the gaps and establish mitigations to cover them, such as upskilling.

Are standard, generic role descriptions effective?

Usually not. Roles should reflect the capability, authority and availability of the individual, seen through the lens of their key relationships, and be reviewed when those relationships shift.

What is the purpose of the communication management approach?

To define the means and frequency of communication with, and feedback from, the project ecosystem — establishing a controlled and bidirectional flow of information.

Where does most organizational communication happen?

Outside formal channels — so provide information in multiple formats and multiple feedback pathways.

Which people sentence signals “manage by exception”?

Decisions made at the most local level where the knowledge resides; and the extent of delegation depending on confidence and trust in key relationships.

Which people sentence signals “learn from experience”?

Valuable knowledge is hidden within a project ecosystem; people factors are best learned through social learning.

Management products 7

What is the purpose of the PID?

It gives the direction and scope of the project and, with the stage plan, forms the “contract” between project manager and project board. It provides the basis for the project's ongoing management.

Name five things inside the PID.

Any of: the nine management approaches, the business case, the project plan, the project management team structure, role descriptions, project controls, user's quality expectations, tailoring decisions.

What is the purpose of the project log?

To capture the continually changing records of issues, lessons, products, quality, risk and other formal or informal actions or events.

Name the six components of the project log.

Daily log, lessons log, risk register, issue register, quality register, product register.

Are management products outputs?

No — they are created solely for the purpose of managing the project. Outputs are the specialist products the project delivers.

Define the project baseline.

The current approved versions of the management products and specialist products that are subject to change control.

What is the three-family test?

“How will X be managed?” → an approach, in the PID. “What is the record or status of X?” → a register or log, in the project log. “How is it going?” → a report.

Business case 13

What is the purpose of the business case practice?

To establish mechanisms to judge whether the project is, and remains, desirable, viable and achievable, as a means to support decision-making in its continued investment.

Define output, outcome and benefit.

Output = the tangible or intangible deliverable of an activity. Outcome = the result of change, normally affecting real-world behaviour and circumstances. Benefit = the measurable improvement resulting from an outcome, perceived as an advantage by the investing organization and contributing to business objectives.

What do outcomes lead to directly?

Benefits — which in turn contribute to business objectives.

Define a dis-benefit, and how it differs from a risk.

A measurable negative consequence of an outcome, perceived as negative by one or more stakeholders. Dis-benefits are expected consequences; a risk is uncertain and may never materialize.

Define a business objective.

The measurable outcomes that demonstrate progress in relation to the organization's strategy, and to which the project should contribute.

What is the purpose of the project brief?

To provide a full and firm foundation for the initiation of the project. It contains the outline business case.

What is the purpose of the benefits management approach?

To define the benefits management actions and benefits reviews that ensure the project's outcomes are achieved and confirm that the benefits are realized — including whether sustainability targets have been achieved.

Where is benefits tolerance documented?

In the business case.

Name the four steps of the business case management technique.

Develop, check, maintain, confirm.

What happens in “develop”?

The project mandate activates starting up a project and is used to develop the initial justification, documented in the outline business case.

Who performs “confirm”, and when?

The business, after the project has closed, as part of a post-project benefits review.

Which costs must the business case include besides development costs?

Any changes to operational costs when the project concludes.

Why can a project succeed and still fail?

Projects are often successful from a delivery perspective but fail from an investment perspective — the outputs are delivered but the outcomes and benefits never materialize.

Organizing 15

What is the purpose of the organizing practice?

To define and establish the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities — the “who”.

Name the three project interests and who represents each.

Business (project executive), user (senior user), supplier (senior supplier).

Name the four management levels.

Commissioning (business layer), directing (project board), managing (project manager), delivering (team manager).

Who is ultimately accountable for the project, and how many are there?

The project executive — one only, appointed first, the single point of accountability. They also secure funding.

What is the senior user accountable for?

Ensuring user needs are specified correctly and the solution meets them; handover and adoption of products; and continued realization of benefits after the project closes.

What is the senior supplier accountable for?

The quality of the products delivered by the suppliers and the technical integrity of the project.

What authority does the project manager have?

Authority to run the project on behalf of the project board within the agreed stage tolerances and constraints.

Is the team manager role mandatory?

No — it is optional and may be performed by the project manager. Team managers may be internal or external.

Who is accountable for project assurance?

Project board members, for their respective areas — business, user and supplier assurance. The board establishes how assurance will be undertaken.

What does project support provide?

Administrative support, meeting and workshop facilitation, advice on tools, planning support, and support to risk, issue and change management.

Distinguish the project team from the project management team structure.

Project team = all people required to allocate time to the project. Project management team structure = project board, project manager, team managers, project assurance and project support. The structure does not itself have authority to direct the project.

Define a work breakdown structure.

A hierarchy of all work to be done, linking the product breakdown structure to the work packages, and helping the project manager structure teams and the boundaries between them.

Name the three organizing management products.

Project management team structure, role descriptions, commercial management approach — all in the PID.

Name the five steps of the organizational design and development technique.

Understand the organizational ecosystem; design the project ecosystem; develop the project ecosystem; manage the ongoing changes to the project ecosystem; transition the project into the organizational ecosystem.

What three aspects does the board consider at transition?

Products, people and learning.

Plans 16

What is the purpose of the plans practice?

To facilitate communication and control by defining the products to be delivered (the what) and the means to deliver them (the who, how, where, and estimates of when and how much) to satisfy the business case (the why).

How many levels of plan are there, and what are they?

Three — project plan, stage plan, team plan. The exception plan is a type of plan, not a fourth level.

Define the project plan.

A high-level plan showing the major products of the project and when, how and at what cost they will be delivered. Created in initiating a project and baselined on board approval.

Define the stage plan.

A detailed plan used as the basis for project management control throughout a stage. Prepared near the end of the previous stage.

Is a team plan mandatory?

No — team plans are optional, produced by a team manager to execute one or more work packages.

When is an exception plan produced?

When a plan is forecast to breach its tolerances, to replace it — at the same level of detail, based on how the project board decides to address the exception.

Define scope.

The sum of product, delivery and management activities represented by an approved plan and its product descriptions and work package descriptions.

Define a dependency.

One product being dependent on another. There are at least two types: internal and external.

What is a schedule?

The sequencing, interrelationships and duration of work packages and their associated tasks. All work packages for a stage must be in the stage's schedule.

What is the planning horizon, and which principle addresses it?

You can only plan in detail as far as you can reliably foresee. Manage by stages addresses it.

What is the purpose of the project product description?

To describe the project's major products and intended purpose, including the user's quality expectations and the acceptance criteria and acceptance methods. Created in starting up a project, refined in initiating a project.

What is a work package description used for?

To describe how one or more products will be produced and delivered, and to pass responsibility formally to a team manager or team member.

What is the minimum number of stages?

Two — an initiation stage and a single delivery stage.

Name the four steps of the PRINCE2 planning technique.

Defining and analysing products; organizing work packages; preparing estimates; preparing a schedule.

In which step is the project product description written?

Defining and analysing products.

What is estimated in “preparing estimates”?

People (skills, effort, when and where needed) and resources (materials, equipment, facilities, access, natural resources, money).

Quality 13

What is the purpose of the quality practice?

To document the user's requirements of the project products and to establish the means by which they will be met.

Define user's quality expectations.

A statement about the quality expected from the project product, captured in the project product description.

Define acceptance criteria.

A prioritized list of criteria the project product must meet before the user will accept it.

Define quality specifications, and where are they stated?

A description of the quality measures applied by those performing quality control and the levels a finished product must meet. Stated in product descriptions.

Define quality tolerance.

The permissible deviation in a product's quality allowed before escalation to the next level of management.

What is the purpose of the quality management approach?

To describe the quality techniques and standards to be applied and the roles and responsibilities for achieving the required quality specifications and acceptance criteria.

Quality register or product register?

Quality register = the quality activities planned or performed and their results. Product register = all products of a plan and their status.

Distinguish quality control from quality assurance.

Quality control monitors the products to check they comply with relevant standards. Quality assurance is an independent check that the project is being run properly — process, not product.

Distinguish quality assurance from project assurance.

Quality assurance is independent of the project, typically corporate. Project assurance is the project board's own, covering business, user and supplier interests.

Name the steps of the quality management technique.

Quality planning — whose activities include gathering user inputs and describing the quality management approach — then controlling quality, then accepting products.

What happens at acceptance?

Ownership or responsibility for the product transfers from the project or supplier to the project board on behalf of the user.

Where do product sustainability requirements go?

Into product descriptions, captured as acceptance criteria or quality specifications.

Define a reviewer.

The person or group responsible for assessing if a product meets its quality or acceptance criteria.

Risk 11

What is the purpose of the risk practice?

To identify, assess and control uncertainties that would affect the project's objectives and, as a result, improve the ability of the project to succeed.

Define a risk.

An uncertain event or set of events that, should they occur, will affect the achievement of objectives — measured by probability combined with magnitude of impact.

Distinguish risk appetite from risk tolerance.

Appetite = the organization's attitude towards risk-taking. Tolerance = a measurable threshold representing the tolerable range of outcomes for an objective at risk.

Distinguish risk owner from risk action owner.

Risk owner manages, monitors and controls all aspects of a risk, including implementing responses. Risk action owner (risk actionee) owns one agreed action.

Define risk exposure.

The degree to which a particular objective is at risk.

Name the risk responses for threats.

Avoid, reduce, transfer, share, accept, prepare contingent plans.

Name the risk responses for opportunities.

Exploit, enhance, share, reject.

Name four decision biases given as examples.

Optimism bias, loss aversion, groupthink, proximity. (There are many types of bias; these four are the examples given.)

Risk management approach or risk register?

Approach = how risk will be managed — procedures, techniques, standards, responsibilities. Register = the identified risks with status and history.

Name the steps of the risk management procedure.

Identify (define context and objectives; identify the risks), assess (prioritize risks; combined risk profile), plan, implement, communicate.

In which step is the risk management approach formulated?

Identify — define context and objectives.

Issues and progress 17

What is the purpose of the issues practice?

To collect and assess issues and control changes to the project's baseline.

Define an issue, and name the five types.

An unplanned event that has occurred and requires management action. Types: problem or concern; event external to the project; business opportunity; request for change; off-specification.

Distinguish a problem from a concern.

A problem has an immediate and negative impact. A concern is an issue whose timeliness and impact need to be assessed.

Define a request for change and an off-specification.

Request for change = a proposal for a change to a baseline. Off-specification = a product that will not meet its quality specifications.

What is the risk of delegating authority for changes too widely?

The overall benefits of the project may be reduced as alignment with the business justification is diluted.

What is a change budget?

Money earmarked to fund approved changes — or a set of authorized constraints within which trade-offs can be made.

Name the five steps of the issue management technique.

Capturing issues, assessing issues, recommending, deciding on changes, implementing changes.

What three questions does “assessing issues” ask?

What type of issue is it? Does this issue affect the project? If so, how?

What is the purpose of the progress practice?

To establish mechanisms to monitor and compare actual achievements against those planned; provide a forecast for the project's objectives and continued viability; and control any deviations causing an exception.

At what levels can progress be monitored?

Work package, stage and project level.

Define an exception.

A situation where it can be forecast that there will be a deviation beyond agreed tolerance levels. It is a forecast breach, not one that has already happened.

Give examples of event-driven and time-driven controls.

Event-driven: end of a stage, completion of the PID, creation of an exception report, end of the financial year. Time-driven: checkpoint report, highlight report.

Who produces a checkpoint report, for whom, and how often?

Team manager to project manager, at a frequency defined in the work package description.

Who produces a highlight report, for whom, and how often?

Project manager to project board, at intervals defined by the board.

What is the purpose of the end project report?

To review how the project performed against the version of the PID used to authorize it.

What happens in step 1 of exception management?

If the project manager can resolve the issue within stage tolerances, no exception report is created.

Name three options open to the board at step 3.

Any three of: accept or reject the recommendation; reallocate overall project tolerances; request an exception plan; escalate to the business layer if project tolerances would be exceeded.

Processes 18

Name the seven processes in order.

Starting up a project, directing a project, initiating a project, controlling a stage, managing product delivery, managing a stage boundary, closing a project.

What is the purpose of starting up a project?

To ensure the prerequisites for initiating a project are established, by answering “do we have a viable and worthwhile project?” — doing the minimum necessary, and preventing poorly conceived ideas from being initiated.

What triggers starting up a project?

The project mandate, from the responsible authority in the business commissioning the project.

What is the purpose of directing a project?

To enable the project board to be accountable for the project's success by making key decisions and exercising overall control, while delegating day-to-day management to the project manager.

Name the four best-known objectives of directing a project.

Authority to initiate; authority to deliver the project product; authority to close; and post-project benefits plans managed and reviewed.

What is the purpose of initiating a project?

To establish solid foundations, enabling the business to understand the work needed to deliver the project product before committing to significant expenditure or resources.

How do initiating a project objectives begin?

“To ensure that there is a common understanding of…” — a useful signpost in list questions.

What is the purpose of controlling a stage?

To assign work, monitor it, handle issues, report progress to the project board and take corrective actions so the stage remains within the tolerances set by the board.

Can controlling a stage be used in the initiation stage?

Yes — normally it is used first after the board authorizes the project, but it can be used during initiation on large or complex projects.

What is the purpose of managing product delivery?

To control the link between the project manager and the team manager, by agreeing the requirements for acceptance, execution, reporting and delivery of specialist products.

In which process does the team manager agree what is to be produced?

Managing product delivery — not controlling a stage.

What is the purpose of managing a stage boundary?

To enable the project manager to give the board enough information to review the success of the current stage, approve the next stage plan, review the updated project plan, and confirm continued business justification and acceptability of the risks.

When is managing a stage boundary performed?

Towards the end of each stage except the final one — and whenever an exception plan is required.

What is managing a stage boundary based on?

Dividing the project into stages. Handling exceptions is a capability it provides, not its basis.

What is the purpose of closing a project?

To provide a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed, and to recognize that the objectives (or approved changes to them) established in the PID have been achieved — and to close the project in an orderly way if closure is premature.

Is closing a project a separate stage?

No — it is carried out as the final part of the last management stage.

Who triggers a premature closure?

The project board — for example if the business case is no longer valid. The process is still executed, possibly tailored.

Name two objectives of closing a project.

Any two of: check user acceptance; ensure the business can support the products; assess benefits already realized; review performance against baselines; address open issues and risks with follow-on recommendations; ensure orderly closure rather than abandonment.
